body_markdown:
According to the 2026 Stack Overflow survey,[65.9% of 17,464](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-select) respondents reported using AI coding assistants or coding agents at work. As AI-assisted development becomes more common, builders increasingly need more than generated code. Platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/en) combine AI-assisted app development with managed databases, authentication, hosting, and deployment.


For non-technical founders and small teams looking to[build full-stack apps](https://floot.com/blog/how-to-build-full-stack-app-with-ai) , the right platform should turn an idea into a working application with saved data and a live URL. This guide compares 12 AI app builders with built-in hosting, examining their infrastructure, pricing, mobile capabilities, and code ownership options.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Managed infrastructure:** Floot provides[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , including PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, email, and hosting, reducing the need to configure these services separately.
- **Floot's connector approach:** Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) supports creating, editing, and publishing apps through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, subject to client permissions.
- **Free to start:** Floot's[pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) include Free with 100 daily building actions, Pro at $25 monthly, and Power at $100 monthly. Hosting allowances and usage limits vary by plan.
- **Code ownership matters:** Floot provides code and data ownership on every plan, with database exports available and full project ZIP downloads on paid plans. Its[export documentation](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) explains the available options.
- **Web and mobile building:** Floot supports[mobile app workflows](https://floot.com/en/mobile) for iOS and Android alongside web publishing. Mobile build allowances vary by plan, and store publishing requires developer accounts and approval.


## **What to Look For in an AI App Builder with Built-In Database**


Not every AI app builder handles databases and hosting the same way. Some platforms provide managed infrastructure for working applications, while others rely on integrations or separate configuration. Understanding these differences matters before choosing a platform, particularly when an application needs user accounts, saved data, payments, and reliable deployment. Pricing and plan information in this comparison was checked in November 2026.


A strong AI app builder with built-in hosting should offer:


- **Managed database** with SQL access or a visual interface for managing application data
- **User authentication** including suitable login methods, account management, and access controls
- **Hosting infrastructure** that supports deployment, SSL certificates, and custom domains
- **Code ownership** through Git synchronization, downloadable project files, or export options
- **Scalable compute** that accommodates growing usage with clearly documented limits and charges
- **Security and compliance controls** including permissions, data protection, and relevant audit reports
- **Mobile support** where needed, with clear distinctions between responsive websites, installable web apps, and native app-store packages


The most practical platforms help teams describe applications in plain language while reducing infrastructure configuration. Teams planning[mobile app development](https://floot.com/en/mobile) should also check whether mobile builds, developer accounts, and store-submission workflows are included or require additional steps.


## **1. Floot**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations.


Floot provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development. Available building capabilities depend on the client's connector permissions.


### **Primary Focus**


Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) lets builders develop applications directly through supported AI assistants instead of requiring a separate AI building environment.


Builders describe what they want, and the connected assistant handles development tasks while Floot provides the[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , including PostgreSQL databases, authentication, file storage, email, and hosting.


Building through a connected assistant uses that assistant's existing subscription or usage allowance rather than consuming a separate pool of Floot AI build credits. Floot's optional AI features may consume separate credits, while hosting usage beyond included allowances can incur additional charges.


### **Key Capabilities**


- [MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) for building through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations
- Managed PostgreSQL databases, authentication, and file storage
- Built-in hosting with SSL certificates and custom-domain support on eligible plans
- [Mobile app conversion](https://floot.com/en/mobile) for iOS and Android, with monthly build allowances
- Code and data ownership on every plan, with database export available and full project ZIP downloads on paid plans
- [Integration ecosystem](https://floot.com/en/integrations) including Stripe, PayPal, Google Analytics, Resend, and Zapier
- Backed by Y Combinator


### **Why Choose Floot**


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , making it relevant for non-technical founders, small business owners, and teams that want working applications without configuring separate infrastructure services.


As of November 2026, Floot's monthly pricing structure includes:


- **Free:** $0 per month, with 100 building actions daily, a one-time $3 hosting credit valid for one year, and 2 mobile builds monthly
- **Pro:** $25 per month, with 1,000 daily building actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, $10 in monthly hosting allowance, and 12 mobile builds monthly
- **Power:** $100 per month, with 5,000 daily building actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, $25 in monthly hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile builds


AI credits apply to eligible Floot AI features, not ordinary connector-based development using an existing assistant. Hosting beyond included allowances is usage-billed.


Floot is particularly useful for builders already using Claude or ChatGPT who want to create applications with user logins, saved data, payments, and managed deployment. Teams comparing different approaches can also explore Floot's[AI builder comparison](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) .


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is a full-stack AI app builder that generates TanStack Start projects for newer applications, with React and Vite used in older projects, paired with Lovable Cloud for backend services.


### **Primary Focus**


Lovable reports that users have created more than 70 million projects since its launch. The platform emphasizes visual design and offers AI-assisted app generation alongside managed backend services.


### **Key Capabilities**


- TanStack Start for newer projects, with React and Vite used in older ones
- Lovable Cloud backend with managed PostgreSQL, authentication, storage, and edge functions
- Two-way Git sync to GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket on every plan, including Free
- Built-in security scans for code review
- 5 build credits daily on the free tier, capped at 30 monthly, with Pro plans at $25 per month


### **App Building Considerations**


Lovable focuses on web applications and does not provide native mobile app generation through its standard building workflow. Teams needing iOS or Android apps should evaluate how the resulting web application would be adapted for mobile distribution.


For teams evaluating connector-based workflows or planning to move an existing project, Floot provides a[migration guide](https://floot.com/blog/how-to-move-your-lovable-project-to-floot) and an overview of[MCP alternatives](https://floot.com/blog/lovable-mcp-alternatives) .


## **3. Bolt**


Bolt is a browser-based AI coding agent from StackBlitz that supports multiple JavaScript frameworks with integrated Bolt Cloud hosting.


### **Primary Focus**


Bolt offers 1 million tokens monthly on its free tier with a 300,000 daily cap. The platform works with React, Vue, Svelte, Next.js, and Angular rather than restricting users to a single JavaScript framework.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Framework flexibility across major JavaScript options
- Bolt Cloud with database, hosting, domains, and Stripe integration
- GitHub sync with commit history preserved
- Mobile app support through Expo
- Unlimited databases on the free tier


### **App Building Considerations**


Bolt operates through a browser-based development environment rather than a traditional locally installed IDE. Teams wanting direct control over development infrastructure or different deployment workflows should compare its environment with their requirements.


For an additional platform-level perspective, see the[Floot comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bolt-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


## **4. Replit**


Replit combines a cloud IDE with an AI Agent and integrated infrastructure for teams that want development environment control alongside AI assistance.


### **Primary Focus**


Replit supports more than 50 programming languages and provides a development environment with terminal access, collaborative editing, and monitoring. Replit Agent can build applications through chat while running browser tests and security checks during development.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Built-in PostgreSQL database with up to 28 days of rollback on Pro plans
- Replit hosting with authentication and monitoring capabilities
- Security Agent scanning capabilities
- Support for web and mobile applications through Expo
- Core plans at $20 monthly, or $18 per month when billed annually


### **App Building Considerations**


Replit offers development environment control alongside conversational app building. Non-technical users should evaluate whether the cloud IDE, terminal access, and configuration options fit their preferred workflow.


Deployment and resource usage can also affect total costs, so teams should review the billing structure for hosted applications.


## **5. Google AI Studio**


Google AI Studio Build mode generates full-stack web applications that can deploy to Google Cloud Run. It also supports native Android app generation through a separate development and testing workflow.


### **Primary Focus**


Google AI Studio deploys full-stack web apps to Google Cloud Run, with Firebase and database services available through configuration. Eligible accounts can publish up to two apps through the free Starter Tier without setting up Cloud Billing.


Its native Android workflow generates Kotlin and Jetpack Compose projects, with browser-based device testing and Google Play testing integration.


### **Key Capabilities**


- React frontend with Node.js server for web applications
- Native Android app generation using Kotlin and Jetpack Compose
- Firebase integration for web app databases and authentication
- GitHub import and code editing capabilities for extending generated web applications
- Standard deployment with Cloud Billing when Starter Tier eligibility or limits do not apply


### **App Building Considerations**


Google Workspace accounts are not eligible for the free Starter Tier. Standard deployment requires a Google Cloud project with billing enabled, although applicable no-cost quotas may still apply.


Native Android applications use a separate workflow from full-stack web applications, and some server-side integrations available to web projects are not supported in Android Build mode.


## **6. Base44**


Base44 is a prompt-to-app platform acquired by Wix in June 2025 for approximately $80 million, with a managed backend that handles databases, authentication, and hosting automatically.


### **Primary Focus**


Base44 generates React and Vite applications with two-way GitHub sync available on Builder plans and above. The backend remains managed, while built-in analytics and security checks help teams monitor usage and review application permissions.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Managed database, user authentication, and backend functions
- GitHub sync on Builder plans and above
- Security scanning for permissions, exposed secrets, and backend functions
- Starter plans at $16 monthly when billed annually
- Usage analytics on all plans, including Free


### **App Building Considerations**


Base44 is web-first but also offers mobile app packaging and publishing workflows for iOS and Android.


Teams should test generated application logic, permissions, and deployment workflows before committing to production use. GitHub integration and certain advanced capabilities require higher subscription tiers.


## **7. v0 by Vercel**


v0 generates Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui code from prompts or images, with deployment through Vercel infrastructure.


### **Primary Focus**


v0 focuses on generating React components and application interfaces while also supporting full-stack application development. Users can turn design mockups into working code and refine generated projects through prompts and visual editing.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Next.js and React code generation with Tailwind CSS
- Design Mode for visual adjustments after generation
- Image-to-code conversion from mockups
- GitHub integration and repository workflows
- Vercel Marketplace integrations including Neon, Supabase, and Upstash


### **App Building Considerations**


v0 supports full-stack application building alongside UI generation. Teams should review how authentication, databases, and backend services are configured through Vercel and its integrations.


The required infrastructure and billing arrangements can vary depending on the selected services.


## **8. Softr**


Softr connects to existing data sources like Airtable, Google Sheets, Notion, and HubSpot to build data-driven applications and portals without code.


### **Primary Focus**


Softr is designed for operations teams that need portals and business applications connected to existing data sources. The platform reports SOC 2 Type II compliance and offers data hosting options in Germany to support EU data-residency requirements.


### **Key Capabilities**


- AI Co-Builder that drafts databases, pages, layouts, and user permissions
- Built-in Softr Databases or connections to external data sources
- Softr MCP integration for building and managing applications through supported AI assistants
- SOC 2 Type II compliant infrastructure
- Basic plans at $19 monthly when billed annually


### **App Building Considerations**


Softr's free plan caps app users at five and does not include custom domains. Teams needing broader user access or branded domains should plan for paid tiers.


Softr is particularly relevant when an application's primary purpose is managing or presenting existing business data through forms, dashboards, and portals.


## **9. Emergent**


Emergent uses a multi-agent system where specialized agents handle design, logic, integrations, testing, and deployment.


### **Primary Focus**


Emergent produces React and Next.js frontends with Python/FastAPI or Next.js API backends and managed MongoDB. The platform supports web applications and mobile development through React Native and Expo.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Multi-agent architecture for different development tasks
- Managed MongoDB with a built-in VS Code environment
- Mobile support through React Native and Expo
- SOC 2 Type I attestation and ISO 27001 certification
- Custom domains, analytics, and application health checks


### **App Building Considerations**


Emergent's credit-based development system makes it important to budget for testing and refinement as well as initial generation.


Teams should also review deployment charges, data handling, and available export options before relying on the platform for production applications.


## **10. Bubble**


Bubble is a visual no-code platform with more than a decade of development, now augmented with an AI app generator that drafts pages and application logic.


### **Primary Focus**


Bubble provides an extensive plugin ecosystem, alongside community resources, agencies, and tutorials. Native iOS and Android applications can be built using its mobile development capabilities.


### **Key Capabilities**


- AI app generator that drafts pages and workflow logic
- Visual editor for detailed customization after generation
- Built-in database and workflow engine
- Native mobile app output for iOS and Android
- SOC 2 Type II compliant infrastructure


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble does not offer conventional application source-code export. Teams needing portable source code should consider this limitation before committing to the platform.


Its visual workflow environment provides detailed control over application behavior, but users should evaluate workload-based pricing and application maintenance requirements.


## **11. Zite**


Zite combines AI app building with visual workflows that appear as flowcharts, similar to workflow automation tools, for teams wanting transparency into backend logic.


### **Primary Focus**


Zite offers unlimited users and apps on the free tier, allowing teams to expand access without per-user app fees. Its visual workflow builder lets non-technical users inspect, test, and modify backend logic without code.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Visual workflow builder with flowchart-style logic inspection
- Built-in no-code database with auto-generated tables
- Unlimited users and apps on the free plan
- SOC 2 Type II compliant infrastructure
- Pro plans at $25 monthly, or $20 per month when billed annually


### **App Building Considerations**


Zite focuses on web applications without native mobile app output. Teams building consumer applications for app stores should verify whether its web-first approach meets their distribution requirements.


Usage limits for records, workflow runs, and AI credits also vary by subscription tier.


## **12. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create, host, and share interactive websites and lightweight applications through ChatGPT, with built-in storage and database capabilities.


### **Primary Focus**


ChatGPT Sites is useful for people already working in ChatGPT who want to turn ideas, documents, or conversations into published websites, dashboards, and lightweight applications without a separate deployment workflow.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Website and lightweight application generation through ChatGPT
- Built-in hosting, database, and file storage
- Sign in with ChatGPT and configurable access controls
- Custom domains where supported and collaborative editing
- Publishing through eligible ChatGPT plans


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites supports working applications with saved data, but its supported runtime, integrations, and hosting limits vary by account and workspace.


Teams building more complex applications should evaluate supported backend services, database requirements, and deployment limitations alongside dedicated full-stack infrastructure platforms.


## **Why Choose Floot for Building and Hosting Full-Stack Apps?**


Floot combines AI-assisted application building with managed infrastructure, making it suitable for founders, operators, and small teams that want working applications without configuring separate backend systems. Its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) lets supported AI assistants handle development tasks while Floot provides hosting, PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, and other application services.


Key advantages include:


- **Familiar building workflow:** Create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, subject to connector permissions.
- **Managed backend:** Use[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) for databases, logins, storage, email, and hosting.
- **Flexible ownership:** Retain code and data ownership, with database exports and paid project downloads.
- **Mobile publishing:** Access[iOS and Android workflows](https://floot.com/en/mobile) , with developer accounts and store approval required.


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , with paid plans providing higher building-action limits, monthly hosting allowances, and additional capabilities. For teams that already use AI assistants, this approach connects application development with managed deployment while keeping AI subscription costs, Floot plan fees, and hosting usage distinct.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What makes an AI app builder suitable for built-in hosting in 2027?**


AI app builders with built-in hosting should provide managed databases, authentication, SSL certificates, and deployment infrastructure with minimal manual setup. They should also offer appropriate security controls, code ownership options, and transparent hosting charges. Floot's[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) includes PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, email, and hosting for full-stack applications.


### **How does Floot work with Claude, Codex, Cursor, and ChatGPT?**


Floot connects to supported AI assistants through MCP, allowing users to create, edit, debug, and publish applications while working in their preferred environment. The assistant handles development tasks, and Floot provides the managed infrastructure. The available actions depend on connector permissions and client capabilities. Users can review the[connector guide](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) for supported setups.


### **Can Floot convert web applications into native iOS and Android apps?**


Yes. Floot supports converting web projects into native app packages for iOS and Android. Its[mobile workflows](https://floot.com/en/mobile) include build options that vary by subscription plan. Publishing to Apple's App Store or Google Play requires the appropriate developer accounts and compliance with store review requirements. Approval is not guaranteed.


### **What integrations are available with Floot?**


Floot supports integrations for payments, analytics, email, and external business services. Its[integration ecosystem](https://floot.com/en/integrations) includes Stripe, PayPal, Google Analytics, Resend, Zapier, and other supported services. Some integrations require separate provider accounts, credentials, or service fees.


### **How much does Floot cost, and can users export their applications?**


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , with Pro at $25 monthly and Power at $100 monthly as of November 2026. Plans have different daily building-action limits, AI credit allowances, hosting allowances, and mobile build limits. Hosting beyond included allowances is usage-billed. Users own their code and data on every plan, can export their database, and can download full project files on paid plans, as explained in the[export documentation](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) .
